title: Welcome to JavaScript Programming
learning_outcomes: Translate a familiar task into inputs, processing steps, and expected outputs.
Write and run JavaScript scripts with variables, operators, strings, and Boolean conditions.
Use branches, loops, and functions to express reusable behavior.
Represent small collections and records with arrays and objects.
Validate input, handle expected errors, and test normal and edge cases.
Organize code with ES modules and explain the limits of local in-memory examples.
module_titles: Work with numbers, text, and conditions
Model data and organize a small program

sections.heading: What is JavaScript Programming?
sections.body: JavaScript programming means writing instructions in JavaScript so a computer can perform tasks. Think of it like giving clear directions to a helper: each instruction tells the helper what to do next.

sections.heading: Why is it useful?
sections.body: JavaScript is widely used to make websites respond to people, and it can also run programs outside a browser. It can support school tools, online shop features, mobile-friendly services, and interactive forms used by organisations and small businesses in Kenya and across Africa.

sections.heading: What can you build or do with it?
sections.body: You will plan a small task, run JavaScript scripts, work with numbers and text, make decisions, repeat instructions, and organise information in arrays and objects. You will combine these skills in a Fictional Reading Shelf Catalog.

sections.heading: How to use these lessons
sections.body: Read the explanation, predict the result of each code example, and then run it yourself. Use the knowledge checks to check your understanding and the activities to practise; compare what happened with what you predicted and investigate any error.

sections.heading: What you need
sections.body: No programming experience is required. You need an approved computer or coding environment with Node.js 20 or newer; internet is useful for setup and reading resources, but the beginner exercises use built-in tools and do not need extra packages.
